name: OpenRouter hosted API router
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, representative model meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct ROUTED TO GROQ, observed 2026-10-14. OpenRouter is a router, not a hoster: the same model id fans out to DeepInfra, Novita, AkashML, Parasail, Cloudflare, SambaNova, Groq, CoreWeave, Google Vertex and Together, each with its own upstream price that OpenRouter passes through with a markup baked into the listed rate. For this one model the 2026-10-14 provider table spans $0.10/$0.32 (DeepInfra Turbo) to $1.04/$1.04 (Together), so price_input/price_output here are the GROQ row - the highest-throughput backend - not the floor. Floor-route price is $0.10/$0.32. Cache-read token pricing differs per upstream ($0.295 on Groq). No single 'OpenRouter price' exists for a model; quote provider+model or nothing.
notes: OpenRouter's own routing telemetry is the measurement: its model pages publish per-provider P50 latency, throughput and uptime measured over real routed traffic (Groq row on llama-3.3-70b-instruct: 0.40s P50 latency, 233 tok/s, 100.00% 3d uptime, observed 2026-10-14). measurement_source 'self' means measured-by-the-service-itself over production traffic - a different claim from 'vendor marketing number' but still first-party. context_window is per-model-per-provider; 131072 is the llama-3.3-70b figure via Groq. Balanced/Nitro/Floor/Exacto routing modes pick different providers for the same request, so 'where does it run' is a routing decision, not a property of the endpoint. Billing goes through OpenRouter regardless of which upstream serves the request.
